originalTitle: US stocks: S&P 500 ends higher as CoreWeave results fuel AI optimism
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know about what happened in the US stock market: the main stock market index, called the S&P 500, went up on Wednesday. This happened because some companies that work with artificial intelligence (AI) had good quarterly results, which made investors happy and willing to buy their stocks. These good results also helped other related companies, like those that make computer chips or run data centers. As a result, investors are now more confident that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates the same next month, rather than raising them. This is good news for the stock market, which is why stock prices went up.

originalTitle: US Treasuries hold gains as softer inflation weakens rate-hike fears
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the prices of US government bonds, also known as US Treasuries, have gone up. This is because the latest numbers on consumer prices (like how much things cost) came in lower than expected, which means people are less worried about inflation (prices rising too fast). As a result, some investors think the Federal Reserve (the group that controls interest rates) might not raise interest rates next month, which is good for bond prices. This is important because it can affect how much it costs to borrow money and how much investors can earn from their investments. Overall, it's a relatively positive sign for the bond market.

originalTitle: US Fed expected to leave rates unchanged next month after soft inflation data
simplifiedContent: The US Federal Reserve, which helps control the economy, is likely to keep interest rates the same at their next meeting. This is because inflation, which is the rate at which prices are rising, has gone down for two months in a row. Even though inflation is still a concern, the decrease in inflation rate reduces the need for the Federal Reserve to take immediate action by increasing interest rates. This decision is important because it can affect the overall economy and the stock market. The Federal Reserve may still consider increasing interest rates in the future, but for now, it seems unlikely to happen at their next meeting.

originalTitle: Corn Jumps as USDA Cuts Yield More Than Expected Amid Heat Waves
simplifiedContent: The price of corn has gone up a lot because the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) said that the amount of corn that will be harvested is lower than expected. This is because of the very hot weather that has been affecting the crops. The USDA's prediction was even lower than what most people thought it would be, which caused the price of corn to jump up suddenly. This is important because corn is a major crop in the US, and changes in its price can have a big impact on the market. The big increase in corn price happened quickly, with the largest jump since June.

originalTitle: US Sells 10-Year Debt at Highest Yields Since Financial Crisis
simplifiedContent: The US government recently sold $42 billion in 10-year loans, called US Treasuries, to investors. This sale resulted in investors earning the highest interest rate on these loans since 2007. This means that investors are now getting paid more to lend money to the US government for 10 years. The high interest rate attracted a decent number of investors who are willing to lend money to the government, but only if they get a higher return. This matters because it shows that investors are seeking higher compensation to lend to the US government, which could indicate changing market conditions.

originalTitle: Oil prices edge up as investors weigh US-Iran talks deadlock against lower demand
simplifiedContent: The price of oil has gone up a little bit. This is happening because investors are considering two things: the fact that the US and Iran are not making progress in their talks, and the fact that people are using less oil right now. The talks between the US and Iran are important because they could affect how much oil is available in the world. Even though people are using less oil, the lack of progress in the talks is causing oil prices to rise. This movement in oil prices is something that investors are paying attention to.
